content.comment_body: Hello, I have the latest version of [product_name] and am trying to upload a program using the SD card on [product_name] with [version_no]. The device restarts each time I attempt to load the program from the SD card, but the program does not get updated. However, updating the program via ethernet works as expected. When I use the SD card to upload a program specifically meant for [version_no], it works without issues.

If you've saved a program to the SD card and inserted it into [product_name], and wish to transfer a new program, make sure to enable the 'Copy to SD card' option. If this step is missed, the program only transfers to memory and will be overwritten by any older program on the SD card after a restart.

I do not intend to transfer another program using a computer. My SD card already contains a program, but I am unable to load it into [product_name]. Every time I click on 'load program from SD Card', the device just restarts.

I'm not completely clear on your issue. If you've transferred a program from PC to SD card, you only need to insert the SD card and restart [product_name]. This should automatically copy the program from the SD card into memory. Afterwards, the SD card can be removed, and it will no longer be needed. However, if you leave the SD card in the device and repeatedly use the 'Load program from SD Card' function, it will reload each time, causing continuous restarts.

I've regularly transferred programs from SD cards to these devices without trouble in the past. I've just noticed that if I select [version_no] for both the hardware and build the program, I can transfer using the SD card. However, it does not work when I use [version_no] as my selected version. Currently, [article_no] and [product_name] [version_no] are being used.
This is confusing to me. Your error description now seems to be about something else entirely.

If the program on your SD card has [version_no] as its hardware setting, then only that hardware version will be able to read it. Earlier versions are not compatible with programs compiled for a newer hardware version. Hope this clarifies things.

Thank you, that's what I suspected. When I choose [version_no], I can update both [version_no] and later models, but not the newer software version directly on older hardware. I tried to find an explanation but couldn't locate clear documentation.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties and confusion when updating [product_name] hardware using SD cards, especially with mismatches between software and hardware versions. Programs compiled with a newer [product_name] software version cannot be loaded onto older hardware, resulting in repeated restarts and failed updates. If the software targets the correct hardware version, the process completes successfully, but lack of clear error messaging and documentation causes user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] hardware to accept and properly update programs from SD cards regardless of compilation software version, or at the very least to provide a clear error message indicating incompatibility.
